driver.rustc_wrapper: RUSTC=<wrapper> that appends the Trust flags to EVERY unit; plain RUSTFLAGS is NOT sufficient because it skips host units (build scripts / proc-macros), which then compile with verification ON and fail the build
driver.rustc_wrapper_source:
#!/bin/sh
# A1 RUSTC wrapper. Applies the Trust lowering configuration UNIFORMLY to every
# compiler unit cargo drives (target crates, proc-macros, build scripts), which
# plain RUSTFLAGS cannot do (RUSTFLAGS skips host units, and those units then
# compile with verification ON and fail the build).
#
# The trust-ir dump sink is attached ONLY to the clean_kernel unit, so no two
# units contend for the same publication name.
#
# TRUSTC and A1_DUMP come from the environment (pinned by the driver).
set -e

# Probe invocations (`-vV`, `--print ...`) must pass through untouched: cargo
# parses their exact stdout and an extra -Z flag can change or reject it.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -vV|--version|--print|--print=*) exec "$TRUSTC" "$@" ;;
  esac
done

EXTRA="-Ztrust-verify=off -Ztrust-ir-lower=on -Cdebuginfo=0"
case " $* " in
  *" --crate-name clean_kernel "*)
    EXTRA="$EXTRA -Ztrust-dump=ir:$A1_DUMP"
    # The pin's ground truth: the literal argv of the subject unit. Anything
    # that could change the emitted IR has to appear here.
    { printf 'ARGV:'; for a in "$@"; do printf ' %s' "$a"; done; printf ' %s\n' "$EXTRA"; } \
      > "$A1_DUMP/clean_kernel.argv"
    ;;
esac

exec "$TRUSTC" "$@" $EXTRA
driver.no_--target_flag: deliberate: with --target, cargo withholds RUSTFLAGS from host units; the wrapper makes the configuration uniform instead
